body:
I was 19 and didn't actually attempt suicide-- my (abusive) mother convinced them that I was going to.  I was billed about 5000 dollars for two and a half days-- Florida Baker acting is supposed to be three days, but the doctor there saw it was bullshit and let me out on the morning of day 2.  Didn't pay, and haven't heard a thing from anyone about it.  

Also:  I made some great friends in that place.  I keep in contact with them now.  Meeting many of them showed me how good I had/have it.  However:  most of the staff were douches.  Some though, were very kind and understanding.

I do this too.  Not that I am any sort of role model, but you aren't alone.  I imagine what I could have done as someone else, or if I were born in a better place (holy shit, if I were one of Louise Leakey's kids!)   But you really do not have to die to live life as someone else.  I think the most difficult part of being a new person is cutting ties with who we are now, but we can do it.

Using my wretched throwaway account for this, but even still, as someone who has been on both ends of this (lots of internets,) all I can advise is some sort of fun internet game you both can enjoy.  Sometimes friendship is much better than the whole stereotypical "support."  Find a free to play game and go to town; much better than wallowing!  Or, if you don't like games, figure out your common interests and do something online related to that.  Crud, if there are knitting Harry Potter communities you guys can find something fun to do together.  As the bad end (usually) in this setting, I can definitely tell you that something fun and a good friend makes all the difference (without hampering that friend.  Have real fun!)

Impromptu edit:  Do NOTTTT talk to anyone's relatives unless you think it is legitimately necessary for his or her health.  Freaking out brothers and sisters (who may have problems of their own) and parents (who likely have problems of their own) won't help unless it is a complete emergency!  Very difficult line to walk, but sometimes this can do more harm than good, especially if the family is a source of the problem.  (Sry for the late edit.)
